selectedAnswer.ending: NEW one active interval. A nested Time Stop declaration rejects before cost; no recursive rolls/turns, extension or queued grant. selectedAnswer.immunityPeer: NEW local interface proposal: an actually source-qualified Time Stop-immune participant is not frozen. Each temporal round supplies it one independent extra turn after the caster in stable prior initiative/ID order, with the same finite personal wallet and no regular refresh. It can move, act, counter during a real later cast, or end the interval through a legal effect. Universal uninterrupted excludes stopped outsiders, not a genuine specific immunity. Timeless Form’s native minute and immunity to time stop/haste/slow are preserved; immunity suppresses only this spell’s freeze/denial contribution, not all time rules. Its operative acquisition, original cast, duration and resumption profile must already be demonstrated. The current index still holds Timeless Form; this proposal does not accept it or manufacture a usable immune actor. That required positive branch is TF192-B01, so Time Stop is unaccepted in this return.
selectedAnswer.interaction: NEW actual voluntary movement, ordinary free/paid object interactions, spells and legal attacks remain useful. Move only along supported legal geometry; handles/doors/items change their same physical records, custody never duplicates. Frozen targets retain actual AC/defenses; stopping time is not Unconscious, an automatic hit/critical or a new attack advantage. A necessary passive defense/check resolves as atomic resistance, not target agency, Reaction or turn. Immediate attack/HP/condition/custody deltas settle once. Normal saves, damage roots, Wounds and concentration consequences remain required; no postponed duplicate payload. Moving a body needs an actually legal carrying/shove/grapple source, capacity and support. Autonomous delayed projectiles/environmental clocks remain paused. Unknown collision/capacity holds that branch.
selectedAnswer.modes: KEEP three placements under one identity. Wizard Illusion and Druid/Mage Transmutation use Action and one explicit d4+1 roll giving 2–5 temporal rounds. Cleric Universal uses Reaction and grants exactly three personal turns. NEW Universal trigger: immediately after a discrete, perceived other-creature Action or movement segment fully resolves within120ft and line of effect, before the next atomic event; never react to another temporal grant, administrative event or your own action. Harm already resolved stays resolved. Its real Reaction and ordinary counter window occur before the interval establishes. No free cross-school mode choice.
selectedAnswer.scope: NEW resolve everyone-but-you literally as a single-world scheduler pause, not a120ft-radius field. Action modes target the caster and use120ft as retained conflicting metadata, not a fabricated area. Universal120ft bounds its triggering event. Offscreen state cannot be assumed absent in a real campaign.
selectedAnswer.turns: NEW each temporal round supplies one caster personal extra turn with one ordinary Action, one Bonus Action only for a genuinely acquired use, one free interaction and current Speed movement. Universal supplies three such turns. These are authentic source-granted extra turns, NEVER regular starts or extra-full-Action grants. No Reaction, recharge, death save, rest, numbered-round entitlement, Haste extra Action or finite resource refresh. Keep stance and shared numbered-round allowances. Personal Action/BA/movement wallets are separate from the interrupted ordinary wallet; retain that original wallet on resume, with actually spent shared Reaction/resource changes. World-clock endpoints and six-second pulses, including the caster’s ordinary deadlines, pause; personal turn ending can end only an explicit this-actual-turn effect. New absolute durations anchor to the paused world instant and first progress after resume. No new numbered ordinary round is fabricated.
